19.t: Working with data: burning fuels in air
q: Which fuel and air supply made the most soot?
Compare the carbon dioxide made by methane with plenty and with little air.
Plenty of air: 95; little air: 60, so about a third less CO₂.
Explain why less air makes carbon monoxide and soot.
Without enough oxygen, combustion is incomplete: some carbon is only partly oxidised to CO, or left as carbon.
Explain why a gas heater in a closed room is dangerous, using these data.
The room’s oxygen runs low, so burning becomes incomplete and makes carbon monoxide, a toxic, colourless, odourless gas. A CO alarm and air supply are needed.
